'''Francesco Damien "Frank" Calegari''' is a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Chicago]] working in [[number theory]] and the [[Langlands program]].

==Early life and education==
Frank Calegari was born on December 15, 1975.<ref name="CV">{{cite web |url=https://math.uchicago.edu/~fcale/WebCV.pdf |title=Frank Calegari (WebCV) |website=Frank Calegari |access-date=September 2, 2024}}</ref> He has both Australian and American citizenship.<ref name="CV"/>

He won a bronze medal and a silver medal at the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] while representing [[Australia]] in 1992 and 1993 respectively.<ref name="imo">{{cite web |url=https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=3156 |title=Frank Calegari |publisher=[[International Mathematical Olympiad]] |access-date=March 6, 2020}}</ref> Calegari received his PhD in mathematics from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 2002 under the supervision of [[Ken Ribet]].<ref name="mathgenealogy">{{MathGenealogy|id=59351}}</ref>

==Career==
Calegari was a [[Benjamin Peirce]] [[Assistant professor|Assistant Professor]] at [[Harvard University]] from 2002 to 2006.<ref name="CV"/> He then moved to [[Northwestern University]], where he was an assistant professor from 2006 to 2009, an associate professor from 2009 to 2012, and a professor from 2012 to 2015.<ref name="CV"/> He has been a professor of mathematics at the University of Chicago since 2015.<ref name="CV"/><ref name="directory">{{cite web |url=https://mathematics.uchicago.edu/people/profile/frank-calegari/ |title=Frank Calegari |publisher=[[University of Chicago]] |access-date=March 6, 2020}}</ref>

Calegari was a [[von Neumann Fellow]] of mathematics at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] from 2010 to 2011.<ref name="ias">{{cite web |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/francesco-damien-calegari |title=Francesco Damien Calegari |date=9 December 2019 |publisher=[[Institute for Advanced Study]] |access-date=March 6, 2020}}</ref>

Calegari was an editor at [[Mathematische Zeitschrift]] from 2013 to 2021.<ref name="CV"/> He has been an editor of ''[[Algebra & Number Theory]]'' and an associate editor of the ''[[Annals of Mathematics]]'' since 2019.<ref name="CV"/><ref name="MZ-board">{{cite web |url=https://www.springer.com/journal/209/editors |publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media]] |title=Mathematische Zeitschrift &#124; Editors |access-date=March 6, 2020 |archive-date=11 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200811052000/https://www.springer.com/journal/209/editors |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="annals-board">{{Cite web |url=https://annals.math.princeton.edu/board |title=Editorial Board |website=Annals of Mathematics |access-date=March 6, 2020}}</ref>

==Research==
Calegari works in [[algebraic number theory]], including [[Langlands reciprocity]] and torsion classes in the cohomology of [[arithmetic group]]s.<ref name="directory"/>

With George Boxer, [[Toby Gee]], and [[Vincent Pilloni]], he proved that all abelian surfaces and genus two curves over totally real fields are potentially modular and satisfy the [[Hasse-Weil conjecture]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Boxer |first1=George |last2=Calegari |first2=Frank |last3=Gee |first3=Toby |last4=Pilloni |first4=Vincent |date=2021-12-01 |title=Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10240-021-00128-2 |journal=Publications mathématiques de l'IHÉS |language=en |volume=134 |issue=1 |pages=153–501 |doi=10.1007/s10240-021-00128-2 |issn=1618-1913|arxiv=1812.09269 }}</ref>

In collaboration with [[Vesselin Dimitrov]] and [[Yunqing Tang]], Calegari proved<ref name="UnboundedDenominators">{{cite arXiv |eprint=2109.09040 |last1=Calegari |first1=Frank |last2=Dimitrov |first2=Vesselin |last3=Tang |first3=Yunqing |title=The Unbounded Denominators Conjecture |date=2021 |class=math.NT }}</ref> the unbounded denominators conjecture of [[A.O.L. Atkin]] and [[Peter Swinnerton-Dyer|Swinnerton-Dyer]]:<ref>{{Citation | last1=Atkin | first1=A. O. L. | last2=Swinnerton-Dyer | first2=H. P. F. | title=Combinatorics (Univ. California, 1968): Proceedings of Symposia in Pure Mathematics, vol. XIX | publisher=American Mathematical Society | year=1971 | chapter=Modular forms on noncongruence subgroups | pages=1–26}}</ref> if a modular form {{math|''f''(τ)}} is not modular for some [[congruence subgroup]] of the [[modular group]], then the Fourier coefficients of {{math|''f''(τ)}} have unbounded denominators. It has been known for decades<ref>{{cite book | last=Shimura | first=Gorō | title=Introduction to the Arithmetic Theory of Automorphic Functions | publisher=Princeton University Press | publication-place=Princeton, N.J | date=1971 | isbn=978-0-691-08092-5 | page=}}</ref> that if {{math|''f''(τ)}} is modular for some congruence subgroup, then its coefficients have bounded denominators.

Also in collaboration with Dimitrov and Tang, he proved the linear independence of {{math|1=1}}, {{math|1=&zeta;(2)}}, and {{math|1=''L''(2,&chi;<sub>&minus;3</sub>)}}.<ref name="trigamma">{{cite arXiv| last1=Calegari | first1=Frank | last2=Dimitrov | first2=Vesselin | last3=Tang | first3=Yunqing | title=The linear independence of {{math|1=1}}, {{math|1=&zeta;(2)}}, and {{math|1=''L''(2,&chi;<sub>&minus;3</sub>)}} | date=2024 | eprint=2408.15403 | page=| class=math.NT }}</ref> This work, along with their work on the Unbounded Denominators conjecture, adds context to the efforts made<ref>{{cite journal | last=Beukers | first=F. | title=A Note on the Irrationality of ζ(2) and ζ(3) | journal=Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society | volume=11 | issue=3 | date=1979 | doi=10.1112/blms/11.3.268 | pages=268–272 | url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1112/blms/11.3.268 | access-date=2025-12-18| url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite conference |last=Beukers |first=Frits |date=1987 |title=Irrationality proofs using modular forms |url=https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1987__147-148__271_0.pdf |book-title=Journées Arithmétiques de Besançon 24-28 Juin 1985 |conference=Journées Arithmétiques - Colloque International du Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique |location=l'Université de Besançon |publisher=Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique | pages=271–273 |access-date=18 December 2025}} (Astérisque, tome 147-148 (1987))</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Rivoal | first1=T. | last2=Zudilin | first2=W. | title=Diophantine properties of numbers related to Catalan's constant | journal=Mathematische Annalen | volume=326 | issue=4 | date=2003-08-01 | issn=0025-5831 | doi=10.1007/s00208-003-0420-2 | pages=705–721 | url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00208-003-0420-2 | access-date=2025-12-18| url-access=subscription }}</ref> to understand [[Roger Apery]]'s proof<ref>{{cite conference |last=Apéry |first=Roger |date=1979 |title=Irrationalité de ζ(2) et ζ(3)  |url=https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1979__61__11_0/ | language=fr
|book-title=Journées Arithmétiques de Lumîny 20-24 Juin 1978 |conference=Journées Arithmétiques - Colloque International du Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique |location=l'Université de Lumîny, Marseille, France|publisher=Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique |pages=1–10 |access-date=18 December 2025}} (Astérisque, tome 61 (1979))</ref> of the irrationality of <math>\zeta(3)</math>.

==Awards==
Calegari held a 5-year [[American Institute of Mathematics]] Fellowship from 2002 to 2006 and a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] from 2009 to 2012.<ref name="CV"/><ref name="homepage">{{cite web|url=https://math.uchicago.edu/~fcale/ |title=Frank Calegari |website=Frank Calegari |access-date=March 6, 2020}}</ref> He was inducted as a [[Fellow of the American Mathematical Society]] in 2013,<ref name="CV"/> and elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-25 |title=UChicago mathematician elected to American Academy of Arts and Sciences {{!}} University of Chicago News |url=https://news.uchicago.edu/story/uchicago-mathematician-elected-american-academy-arts-and-sciences |access-date=2025-04-28 |website=news.uchicago.edu |language=en}}</ref> He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-27|title=Exceptional scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society|url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2026/05/new-fellows-announcement-2026/|access-date=2026-05-31|website=Royal Society|language=en}}</ref>

Calegari was a plenary speaker at the 2022 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], where he gave a lecture entitled "30 years of modularity since [[Fermat's Last Theorem]]."<ref>{{Cite web |title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers {{!}} International Mathematical Union (IMU) |url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=Frank+Calegari |access-date=2025-04-28 |website=www.mathunion.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EDsK-8SBx-g |title=Frank Calegari: 30 years of modularity: number theory since the proof of Fermat's Last Theorem |date=2022-08-15 |last=International Mathematical Union |access-date=2025-04-28 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

Calegari was awarded the 2026 [[Cole Prize]] in Number Theory jointly with [[Vesselin Dimitrov]] and [[Yunqing Tang]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7548 Frank Nelson Cole Prize for Number Theory 2026]</ref>
